articles.title: The Steam Frame Shouldn't Work - Here's Why It Does
articles.summary: Lock your cloud storage before AI can scrape it. Get started now with Proton Drive at no cost:
body: Valve's Steam Frame promises your entire Steam library on a standalone headset - but every one of those games was built for x86 processors, and the Frame runs an ARM chip straight out of a smartphone. The trick that makes it possible is FEX, a translator Valve has quietly funded for years that recompiles your games live, while you play. We break down how it works, what it costs in performance, and why it matters way beyond VR with Pierre-Loup Griffais, one of the Valve engineers behind SteamOS.

points: GPU prices have become a meme, with NVIDIA leading the pack at (on average) 70% over listed MSRP for its consumer and gaming video cards.
AMD and Intel are likewise running higher prices than previously, reaching new highs for GPU prices in our year-long series tracking them.
November of 2025 seems like it was the best time to buy, with prices now climbing even past what we saw in February of 2026.
This continues to get worse with thanks to the ongoing DRAM availability crisis thanks to AI data center buildout -- one largely caused by the very companies that make the consumer GPUs.
